We have mass spec: m/z 193.1103 (M+? likely molecular ion). So molecular weight ~193.11. The carbon NMR peaks: 166.40, 144.78, 132.00, 130.07 (x2), 127.80 (x2), 52.24, 49.55, 43.55, 19.23.

We need to deduce structure. The formula we guessed earlier C11H15NO2 (mass: C11=132, H15=15, N=14, O2=32 => total 193). Yes matches mass 193.11. So formula C11H15NO2.

Now need to propose SMILES. Use NMR data: carbon shifts: 166.4 suggests carbonyl (ester or amide). 144.78 aromatic? maybe aromatic carbon attached to hetero. 132,130,130,127,127 are aromatic carbons. So aromatic ring present (6 carbons). 52.24,49.55,43.55 are aliphatic carbons attached to hetero (C-O, C-N). 19.23 is methyl.

Thus likely an aromatic amide or ester with side chain.

C11H15NO2 could be N-methyl-4-methylphenyl acetate? Let's compute: p-tolyl acetate (C9H8O2? Actually p-tolyl acetate: C9? Wait p-tolyl acetate = C9? Let's compute: C6H4-CH3 (C7H7) plus OCOCH3 (C2H3O2) total C9? Actually C6H4-CH3 = C7H7, plus OCOCH3 adds C2H3O2 => total C9? That's C9? Let's sum: C7+2= C9? That's C9? Wait we need C11. So maybe N-methyl-4-methylbenzamide? That is C9? Let's compute: benzamide C7H7NO? Actually benzamide C7H7NO? No benzamide is C7H7NO? Actually benzamide formula C7H7NO? Let's compute: C6H5CONH2 = C7H7NO? plus O? Actually C6H5 (C6H5) + CONH2 (C1O1N1H2) => C7H7NO? plus O? Wait carbonyl O included. So C7H7NO? plus O? Actually carbonyl O is part of CONH2. So total C7H7NO? plus O? Let's compute: C6H5 = C6H5, plus C=O (C1 O1) plus NH2 (N1 H2) => C7 H7 N1 O1? plus O? Already accounted. So C7H7NO? That's C7H7NO? Not correct. Anyway.

Our formula C11H15NO2 suggests maybe an amide with aromatic ring and alkyl chain.

Consider N-methyl-4-methylbenzamide: C9? Let's compute: aromatic ring C6H4 (since substituents at para: CH3 and CONHCH3). So base C6H4. Add CH3 (C1H3) => C7H7. Add CONHCH3: carbonyl carbon C1, O1, N1, CH3 (C1H3). So total C9? Actually add C1 (carbonyl) + C1 (methyl) = C2, plus N and O. So total carbons: 6+1+2 =9. So C9H? Not enough.

We need 11 carbons. Maybe phenoxyacetamide? e.g., phenoxyacetamide: C8? Not.

Consider phenacetyl amine? Let's think.

Carbonyl at 166 ppm typical for amide carbonyl (around 165-175). So likely amide.

Aromatic ring 6 carbons accounted. So remaining carbons: 11-6 =5 aliphatic carbons. One carbonyl carbon (already counted 166). So remaining 4 aliphatic carbons: 52,49,43,19. Those could be: O-CH2 (around 50), N-CH3 (around 30-40), maybe CH2 attached to N (around 45), and a methyl (19). So maybe structure: phenoxyacetyl dimethylamine? Let's test: phenoxyacetyl dimethylamine: O-Ph-O-CH2-CO-N(CH3)2. Carbons: phenyl 6, O-CH2 (1), carbonyl carbon (1), two N-methyls (2). Total 10. Need 11, maybe plus extra methyl on aromatic (para methyl). So p-methyl phenoxyacetyl dimethylamine? That would be C11? Let's compute: phenyl with para methyl adds one carbon (makes 7 aromatic carbons). Then O-CH2 (1) carbonyl (1) two N-methyl (2) = total 11. Yes.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1)OCC(=O)N(C)C . Let's check formula: Cc1ccc(cc1)OCC(=O)N(C)C. Count: aromatic ring C6, plus methyl on ring C1 =7, O-CH2-CH2? Actually O-CH2-? O-CH2-? The O attached to aromatic O? Wait O attached to aromatic carbon: phenoxy group: O-CH2-? Actually OCH2C(=O)N(CH3)CH3. So O-CH2 (C1) then carbonyl carbon (C1) then two N-methyls (C2). Total carbons =7+1+1+2=11. Hydrogens: aromatic ring with methyl: C6H4 (since one O substituent, one methyl) plus methyl (CH3) = C7H7? Actually phenyl with O and CH3 substituents: C6H4 (two substituents) + CH3 (on ring) = C7H7. O-CH2 adds CH2 (2 H). Carbonyl carbon no H. Two N-methyls each CH3 (6 H). Total H =7+2+6=15. N1 O2. So formula C11H15NO2 matches! Good.

Now check carbon NMR shifts: aromatic carbons: 144.78 (C attached to O), 132,130,130,127,127 typical. Aliphatic: O-CH2 attached to aromatic O ~ 70 ppm? But we have 52.24 maybe O-CH2 attached to carbonyl? Actually O-CH2 attached to aromatic O is benzylic O-CH2, typical ~ 70. But we have 52. Could be CH2 attached to carbonyl (alpha to carbonyl) ~ 40-45. But we have 49.55 and 43.55. The N-methyls around 30-40, but we have 19.23 for methyl (maybe aromatic methyl). The N-methyls maybe 30-40 but not present? 52 maybe O-CH2. 49.55 maybe N-CH3? 43.55 maybe other N-CH3? But N-CH3 typical ~30. However maybe due to N,N-dimethyl amide shift ~ 30-40. 49 seems high. Could be CH2 attached to O and carbonyl (O-CH2-CO) shift ~ 65. Not 52. But still plausible.

Thus SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1)OCC(=O)N(C)C

We should validate: earlier we validated "Cc1ccc(cc1)OCC(=O)N(C)" which is missing one methyl on N (only N-methyl). That formula would be C10H13NO2? Not correct. The SMILES we propose has N(C)C (dimethyl). Let's validate.
